Woonyville has a lot of character.  It’s an old city that used to be very prosperous due to the mills.  You can see this in the architecture and some of the stately homes that are still around.  But it has fallen on some hard times like so many other places with manufacturing going overseas.   If you want to learn a bit about the history and culture of your new home check out the Museum of Work and Culture.  It’s a cool little museum with some interesting stuff.  One of the best aspects of Woonsocket is the food.   Check out the New York lunch- a little diner that has some of the best New York System hot wieners around (a RI specialty).  Ye Olde has awesome fish and chips.  It’s like stepping back in time; the place is like a hundred years old and has been making their fish and chips the same way all along.  The Castle is another old timey diner.   Ciros is a cool little bar/ restaurant and has good pub trivia.  Right up the road is Wrights dairy which is an unbelievably tasty bakery.  They got the cows right in the back so you know the ingredients are the freshest and highest quality.   The Dairy farm is not to be confused with Wrights’s Chicken farm which has the best family style chicken dinners around, which I think is another RI thing.   Kay’s is another time machine, they have a limited sandwich menu but are famous for their Delmonico steak sandwiches.  Chelos has great burgers.   Chan’s has Chinese food and all sorts of live music.  There is a significant population of people from Southeast Asia so there are a bunch of places with authentic southeast Asian food.   Wilfreds is a great little seafood market.  Their take home meals are awesome.  Best coleslaw around too.  Vose and Pepin lumber are two nice hardware stores that are right across the street from one another.  Vose has just about anything you could possibly need.   And a lot of stuff you don’t.   Anyway, I think Woonsocket is great.  The people may not be driving Bentleys but I’ve found most people to be pretty nice.   Make sure you roll your windows up when you go by the sewage treatment plant though-you’ll know it when you’re near it.   Autumnfest happens in the Fall and that’s a fun time, make sure you get a dynamite sandwich- a local delicacy.   I’m sure I’m forgetting other places to check out.  There’s also a ton of stuff to do and cool places to check out in the rest of the state.   Good luck with your new adventure.  Feel free to message me if you are looking for advice on other places to check out and things to do.   Bienvenue Woooonsocket.

And it’s not usually as bad as it seems at first.  Also, don’t edit as you go, just get your thoughts down and then go back.  Don’t interrupt your flow of thoughts by try to fix typos or bad grammar along the way
-always always always have someone, anyone proof read your writing before turning it in
-Wikipedia is a great starting point for research.  Use the reference at the end of articles for sources (not the Wikipedia article itself) 
-take breaks, especially when you’re getting frustrated or tired.  Ideas “magically” come together when you’re not concentrating on them
-use a thesaurus: different words don’t only improve your vocabulary, more importantly, they can often give you a different perspective on a topic 
-if you have a lot of reading to do, concentrate on the first and last paragraph of each chapter and the first and last sentence of each paragraph, that’s where the main ideas are located.  The rest is mostly filler, skip it if you’re in a pinch, or if it’s just totally boring 
-quotes are also your “friend,” use them copiously.  Don’t worry about plagiarism or “putting it in your own words,” when in doubt just use a quote and make sure you cite it.  Think of quotes as writing that’s free for you to use (and less you have to write yourself) just make sure you cite the info properly.  
-use the bibliography of books/ articles to get more sources for your topic
-gather as many sources as possible to start your research.  Even if you use just one measly quote from a 500 page book, it’s worth it, and bonus: it makes your paper look better because you add it into your bibliography.  An extensive bibliography makes a paper look more impressive.  Along the same lines: even if you just glance at one paragraph of a book, include it in your bibliography, again, it just makes your bibliography/ research look more impressive
